solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Played a part in curriculum originally intended to educate

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: did is a past tense of do, as in 'did Hamlet' for played him
Act I is one part of a play
first letter of curriculum

explanation.surface: A teacher's role in drawing up a school syllabus, meant to be instructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A part' is read theatrically: the first act of a play, written ACT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic describes teaching material designed to instruct, often with a moral purpose.

clue.text: Judge killed by Mob set back detective's case

indicators.note: set back means moved backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: iced is gangster slang for murdered, the sort of killing a mob carries out
outer letters of detective

explanation.surface: A judge is murdered by gangsters, and a detective's investigation is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Judge' the murder victim; it is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a matter is to decide it, settling the question one way or the other.

clue.text: Saved having had organ removed?

blocks.note: first meaning: rescued
second meaning, read whimsically

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into DE (removal) and LIVERED, a jokey coinage flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delivered is to be rescued or set free from danger, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Angry and embarrassed about interminable submission full of self- citations?

indicators.note: something interminable has no ends, so the first and last letters of the word go
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: cross is a synonym for angry
embarrassed people go red in the face
deference is respectful submission to another

explanation.surface: An academic fumes and blushes about a never-ending thesis that keeps quoting its own author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submission' looks like a thesis handed in; here it means yielding respectfully to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A text cross-referenced throughout points readers to other places within itself, much like citing oneself.

clue.text: Find fault with emphatic dancing out of time

indicators.note: out of means lacking, so the letter for time leaves the word
dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A critic objects to energetic dancing that is off the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to call into question or discredit, as in impeaching a witness's honesty.

clue.text: Teach group at home in the main

definitions.text: group at home in the main

blocks.note: first meaning: to train or educate, as a verb

blocks.clueFragment: group at home in the main
blocks.note: second meaning: a shoal of fish, 'the main' being the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic term for the sea, so the group living there is a gathering of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train them, and a school is also the collective noun for fish swimming together.

clue.text: They may refute claim of nobleman about plenty supporting English king

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the rest
in a down answer a supporting piece holds up from below, so it is placed after the one it supports

blocks.note: count's, the possessive of a European nobleman
E is the abbreviation for English
rex is Latin for king
ample means plenty

explanation.surface: A noble's land claim is challenged, with plenty of evidence behind an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 'of nobleman' is read as letters that go around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterexample is a single case that disproves a general proposition, so several can refute a claim.

clue.text: Outstanding victory secured by own goal

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast inside it

blocks.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A football team clinches a remarkable win thanks to an opponent's own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the victory; here it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still owing, not yet settled.

clue.text: Extend personal support immediately to protect name

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a leg is what supports a person
N is the abbreviation for name
then means next in time, straight after

explanation.surface: Offer someone your backing at once so that their reputation is shielded.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to make it longer, which is to extend it.

clue.text: Number one hit captures something kids will play

indicators.note: to capture is to take inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to bop is to hit
number one is a nursery euphemism for urinating

explanation.surface: A chart-topping single features a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one hit' reads as a chart success; split it, and 'number one' is a child's word for a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Bo-peep is the old name for peekaboo, a hiding game played with small children.

clue.text: Senior director accepts limitations of legal instrument

indicators.note: limitations are the boundaries, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: chief executive officer, the most senior director
outer letters of legal

explanation.surface: A company boss agrees to the restrictions of a legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a legal document in this setting; it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Wealth of person paid to play rugby union?

blocks.note: a professional player is paid to play
fusion is a joining together, a union

explanation.surface: Asks how rich a professional rugby union player gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby union' is the name of a sport, but the clue breaks the phrase so union is its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A profusion is an abundance, so a wealth of something is a profusion of it.

clue.text: Destroy Dutch property bordering Virginia

indicators.note: to border something is to lie along its edges, so one piece flanks the other

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
an estate is a piece of property
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A demolition plan targets a Dutch-owned estate next to Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: To devastate is to lay waste, to destroy completely.

clue.text: Mean drunk filled with tension

blocks.note: first meaning: stingy with money
second meaning: intoxicated, in informal use
third meaning: tense or taut

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: 'filled with tension' is a third sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stingy, inebriated, and tautly stretched, three common senses of one adjective.

clue.text: What is behind quarrel on radio

indicators.note: on the radio words are heard rather than read, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: a breach is a rift or quarrel between people

explanation.surface: Asks what lies behind a row being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What is behind' sounds like asking for a cause; it is literal: the breech is the buttocks or rear part.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the back part of something, such as a gun barrel or a person's rump.

clue.text: Bearer of message with enough strength to follow standard

blocks.note: par is the standard score, as in golf
able means having the power to do something

explanation.surface: A courier strong enough to carry the flag behind the standard-bearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearer of message' suggests a messenger; it is a story that carries a moral.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a simple story told to convey a moral or spiritual lesson.

clue.text: Who may make Manhattan veto proposal?

blocks.note: to bar is to forbid, to veto
a tender is a formal offer or proposal

explanation.surface: Asks who could build Manhattan by blocking a planning proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: Manhattan is a cocktail of whiskey and vermouth, not the New York borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender mixes drinks, and a Manhattan is a classic cocktail he or she might shake.

clue.text: Virgin Trains regularly sacked inept guards

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept
something sacked is ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled
to guard is to stand around something, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
second, fourth and sixth letters of trains

explanation.surface: A rail company fires its incompetent security staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin Trains' is a British rail operator; split off, 'Virgin' is the definition as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine means untouched and unspoilt, in its original state, as in virgin snow.

clue.text: Right to put on new clothes?

blocks.note: first meaning: to set right a wrong, as a verb
second meaning, read playfully

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense as a split: RE (again) plus DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a grievance is to remedy it, putting the wrong to rights.

clue.text: Genie possibly found in bottle

blocks.note: first meaning: a supernatural being, of which a genie is one example
second meaning: courage, as in British slang 'he lost his bottle'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a genie in its bottle; but bottle is British slang for nerve or courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a kind of spirit, and spirit also means courage or mettle, which British speakers call bottle.

clue.text: Spoil unruly minx finally giving up new indulgence

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word
giving something up means letting it go, so that letter is dropped
to spoil something is to ruin its form, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of minx
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Pampering a badly behaved young woman, who in the end gives up a new treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' looks like the indulgence itself; it is the anagram signal, and N comes out of UNRULY before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury is a costly pleasure, an indulgence rather than a necessity.

clue.text: Grant permission to disrupt silence

indicators.note: disrupting something breaks its order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Authorising someone to break the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To license is to give formal authorisation, the verb spelt with S in British usage.

clue.text: Go regularly to listen

blocks.note: first meaning: to be present at, as with school or church
second meaning: to pay attention

explanation.surface: Turning up habitually to hear something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' usually picks alternate letters; here it is plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is both to be present habitually somewhere and to give heed to what is said.

clue.text: Comment unfavourably on list of presidential candidates perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to criticise harshly, informal British usage
second meaning: a roster of candidates put forward together

explanation.walkthrough: To slate something is British slang for panning it; the US sense is a ticket of nominees.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics slate a bad play, and a party puts up a slate of nominees for election.

clue.text: Developer of computer program failing to terminate

indicators.note: something that fails to terminate never reaches its end, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: an applet is a small computer program

explanation.surface: A software developer whose program will not stop running.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the company, the maker of the Macintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple is the technology firm that designed and built the Mac and other personal computers.

clue.text: Office-holder's intent on profit we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the words are spelt by how they are spoken

blocks.note: bent on means intent on, and income is profit, so 'bent' goes on (after) 'income'

explanation.surface: A politician in power is set on making money, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intent on profit' is read as BENT placed on INCOME, that is after it; spoken together they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An incumbent is the current holder of an office or post.

clue.text: Crushing effect of behaviour by naughty child

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
an action is a piece of behaviour

explanation.surface: The devastating result of a badly behaved child's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaction is the state of being tightly pressed or wedged together, a crushing compression.

clue.text: What typically projects keenness by learner?

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
edge means sharpness or keenness

explanation.surface: Asks what shows enthusiasm in a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projects' sounds like showing an attitude; it means sticks out, as a shelf does.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf jutting out from a wall or cliff face.

clue.text: Corrects unique feature of emblem

blocks.note: a distinctive trait: it has EM at both ends
the word emblem begins and ends with the same two letters

explanation.surface: Fixes the one distinctive detail of a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: Emblem starts and finishes with EM, so its odd feature is 'EM ends'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct errors in it, typically before publication.

clue.text: Deliberate course of action ending in bloodshed

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a measure is a planned course of action
last letter of bloodshed

explanation.surface: A calculated plan that ends in violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured describes something careful and considered, done slowly and on purpose.
